review_notes: I read the whole file and looked at the repeated blocks. All of them are dual pairs: Algebra and Coalgebra isoMk, iso_of_iso, functorOfNatTrans, equivOfNatIso, and Initial.right_inv and Terminal.left_inv (Lambek's lemma). I did not open any other source files. I found no shared lemma that would be a clear improvement. The dual proofs differ in the direction of composition and in where F.map is applied. Merging them would need a bridge through opposite categories, with an equivalence between Coalgebra F and (Algebra F.op)ᵒᵖ. That bridge costs more than the short rewrite chains it would replace. The Algebra and Coalgebra isoMk proofs are 3–4 line rewrites plus simp, which is routine. The two homEquiv_naturality lemmas are each a single 2–3 step rw, so they count as short calculations. The repeated `NatIso.ofComponents fun X => isoMk (Iso.refl _)` terms and the equivOfNatIso bodies are thin wrappers around the existing API. One uncertainty: a more elaborate unification through the opposite-category dual could exist, but I could not show that it would be a net gain under the rubric.
